name: Reflective STN, Nintendo DMG-01 (Retro Display Lab reconstruction)

attribution.changes: Values copied into one JSON profile. The contrast tables (stn.target_q, drift_per_frame, optical, anchors, corrections) are recomputed by tools/dmg01_wheel.mjs with the source's own solver at every 0.01 of the wheel from 0.85 to 1.08, with the optical calibration continued beyond the nominal shades. Used without the pixel aperture, the passive-matrix crosstalk and the row-latch scan-out, which belong to the 160x144 dot grid.

panel.ref: Nintendo Game Boy technical data (DMG-DIMENSIONS-01); DMG drive record dmg-drive-v1.json

palette.interpolation: linear light, piecewise between the five states
palette.ref: BGB, The reality of DMG colors (DMG-COLOR-01): central-patch samples

drive.mapping: shade = floor(3 (1 - luma) + 0.5), luma = Rec.709 weights on the encoded sRGB value (Retro Display Lab gameboy_drive_index)
drive.note: inferred from LD0/LD1 plus four CPG pulses per line; exact LH5077 switching truth table unavailable

contrast.note: 30 kohm potentiometer between ground and the approximately -19 V LCD rail, with its wiper feeding IR3E02 VR
contrast.range: x0.85 to x1.08: a rough reading, not a calibration: -11 V and -14 V at the ends of the wheel on a faulty unit with an old needle meter, the measuring point not stated; -13 V for good contrast on another unit (chipmusic.org, "DMG screen stuck on max contrast?", 2015). The best available; the source supports 0.88 to 1.08.
contrast.solved: every 0.01 by tools/dmg01_wheel.mjs with the source's solver; the source tabulates 0.88, 1.00 and 1.08 only

stn.layout: drift_per_frame[(condition*4 + shade)*bins + bin], bin over director coordinate q in [0, 1]
stn.method: overdamped 1D Frank-Oseen/Ericksen-Leslie reduction with finite anchoring; 15-wavelength sliced Jones round trip through two polarizers and reflector
stn.claim: No parameter is presented as a measurement of an unaged DMG-LCD-01 or DMG-LCD-06 cell. Unknown analogue levels, material identity, and polarizer spectra remain bounded reconstructions.
stn.optical_range: optical states continue below 0.25 (lighter than nominal white) and above 1 (darker than nominal black), linearly in luminance; used for the drive-change projection and for reports. The colour comes from stn.color.
stn.coordinate: q = mean sin^2(tilt) through the cell, 0 at the unpowered rest, 1 at the source's high-bound black (x1.08, shade 3); 116 solved resting states along it (both branches at every wheel position), blended only between them

metastable.basis: assumed: geometric middle of 0.1-1 s, the erasure time of metastable twisted textures by defect nucleation and propagation (US 6,867,836, 180-degree texture, thickness-dependent); no DMG or STN measurement found
metastable.rule: per point, once per screen update: a point resting nearer its temporary state than its stable one takes the stable state with chance 1 - exp(-frames * viscosity factor / (tau * refresh)); which state is stable: the lower free energy (the source's functional)
metastable.evidence: BGB: as in reality, the lightest shade is the LCD disabled color; videos of real DMGs turned down show a plain screen, no lasting ghost

color_basis.method: BGB's five measured colours, chosen by the solver's luminance of each crystal state: linear light between shades; lighter than white, toward the LCD-disabled colour and clamped there; darker than black, black dimmed by the luminance ratio
color_basis.why_not_the_spectrum_hue: the five colours lie nearly on one line, so a colour conversion fitted to them extrapolates hue (lime, navy) that no photo of a real DMG shows (v0.32.0)
color_basis.ref: BGB, The reality of DMG colors: colour-accurate light, ColorChecker-corrected to true colour and brightness in sRGB, 1/60 s, defocused, averaged; contrast wheel: the lightest shade is the LCD disabled color, darker than normal is darker than the darkest normal shade

temperature.law: drift per frame scaled by response_scale × exp(activation_K (1/293.15 - 1/T))

retention.ref: Nakazono et al. (Merck Japan, 1994) sticking-voltage regression; the optical gain is an explicit bridge (Retro Display Lab)

shadow.ref: Retro Display Lab reflector shadow (DMG-APERTURE-01), reference-image matched

geometry.note: DMG glass thickness not published; 1.1 mm is the thickest of the common small-STN options (0.4/0.55/0.7/1.1 mm), the same front stack as the TN profiles (assumed)

response.measured: mean 10–90% response in shown brightness over the 12 shade changes at 25 °C: 149 ms (100–201 ms per change), with the 257-bin tables of tools/dmg01_wheel.mjs; the tables alone give 70 ms (50–100 ms); until v0.31 the 65-bin tables needed 0.64
response.basis: no DMG measurement exists; matched to the era's published STN figures, not to a DMG panel
refs: Sharp, 1997 press release: conventional STN 300 ms (10–90% rise plus fall), i.e. about 150 ms per change
Hitachi, 1996 (Nikkei): conventional STN 300 ms rise plus fall, 10–90%
Sharp LM32019T STN module datasheet: rise 190 ms, fall 210 ms
Period small STN modules: 100–200 ms (Japanese DMG-recreation notes, unmeasured)

limitations: The target is a healthy period-DMG appearance reconstructed from DMG-specific evidence and contemporary STN measurements, not a surviving aged specimen
No identified original panel analogue waveform, fill material, or full voltage-transmission curve; these remain bounded literature reconstructions
Response varies with specimen, temperature, contrast wheel, and aging

LH5076/LH5077 analogue output resistance and the DMG electrode mask remain unavailable; WS5 propagates comparable period-driver, ITO, cell-gap, and dielectric ranges rather than claiming a measured Nintendo coefficient

lens.note: Clear "high-impact plastic" window in the front shell (Game Boy Modding, No Starch), its frame printed on the underside (assumed). Index of acrylic (PMMA, n 1.49, assumed; polycarbonate would be 1.585 and mirror slightly more). 1.0 mm is an upper estimate: replacement lenses are sold at 1.0 mm (Hand Held Legend) and owners report they sit higher than the stock lens. The 1.0 mm air gap to the LCD is not published (assumed). The measured palette is taken as seen through the lens, so the lens does not dim it again.
lens.effect: glare from three parallel surfaces (lens front, lens back, LCD front); the printed frame's shadow falls across the air gap

scratches.basis: Wear varies by unit; no DMG lens has been measured. Typical scratch sizes on clear plastics and coatings: light wiping/car-wash marring 'only a few microns' wide and deep (automotive coatings review); micro-scratches on polycarbonate about 4.7 um wide and 3-4 um deep by profilometry; fracture scratches 25 um to over 1 mm. Densities, lengths and swirl radii (a cloth's circular strokes) are assumed. Groove cross-section: a circular segment of the width and depth (assumed).
refs: An Overview of the Scratch Resistance of Automotive Coatings (Coatings 2012, 2(4), 221; https://www.mdpi.com/2079-6412/2/4/221)
Nanovea, Micro Scratch Depth & Area by Non-Contact Profilometry (https://nanovea.com/micro-scratch-depth-measurement-using-3d-profilometry/)
scratches.effect: glints where a scratch runs crosswise to the half-way direction between the light and the eye (arcs around the lamp's reflection); the scratches sit on the lens front, gap + thickness above the image, so they shift against it when the view tilts

contrast_solution_note: temporary: the other resting state where a shade has two (q, luminance relative to normal white, free energy above the stable one)

reflector.source: Brick Boy emulator developer (fugudaro/kathoc), measured from close-up images of LCD modules: grains 0.3-0.5 dot, non-directional, amplitude total ±3.9% (Time Extension, Aug 2026, https://www.timeextension.com/news/2026/08/the-most-gorgeous-game-boy-emulation-ive-ever-seen-brick-boy-goes-the-extra-mile-to-copy-the-consoles-nostalgic-display); which unit and photos not stated
reflector.basis: grain 0.4 dot (0.118 mm at the 0.294 mm pitch from Nintendo's 47 mm / 160 dots); ±3.9% read as the peak of the variation (assumed reading); value noise, a multiplicative reflectance where the light bounces, halfway between entry and exit
reflector.effect: a fixed paper-like texture, strongest in light areas (multiplicative), averaged out where a screen pixel is wider than the grain
